name: Dim Sum Platter
instructions: Mix shrimp, pork, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil.
Place 1 tsp filling in center of each wrapper.
Pleat and seal edges carefully.
Steam for 10 minutes until translucent.
Serve with soy sauce and chili oil.
tips: Keep wrappers covered with damp cloth to prevent drying.

name: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)
instructions: Mix ground pork with minced aspic and seasonings.
Wrap carefully, pleating the top tightly to seal the soup inside.
Steam for 8–10 minutes until translucent.
Serve immediately with black vinegar and ginger shreds.
Bite a small hole first to suck the soup, then eat the rest.
tips: The aspic melts into soup during steaming — this is what makes xiaolongbao special.

name: Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing)
instructions: Mix flour and hot water into a soft dough, rest 30 minutes.
Roll out, brush with sesame oil, sprinkle green onions and salt.
Roll up, coil into a spiral, then flatten again.
Pan-fry until both sides are golden and crispy.
Cut into wedges and serve.
tips: The multiple layers create the signature flaky texture.

name: Turnip Cake (Lo Bak Gou)
instructions: Cook shredded daikon until soft, mix with rice flour and seasonings.
Pour into a greased pan and steam for 40–45 minutes until set.
Cool completely, then slice.
Pan-fry slices until golden and crispy on both sides.
Serve with chili sauce or soy sauce.
tips: Best when steamed a day ahead so it firms up for easier slicing.

name: Tomato Egg Stir-Fry (Xihongshi Chao Jidan)
instructions: Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
Scramble eggs quickly in hot oil until just set, then remove.
Stir-fry tomatoes until they release juices and soften.
Add a pinch of sugar, return eggs, and toss gently.
Finish with green onion and serve over rice.
tips: A true Chinese home classic — sweet-savory tomatoes and soft eggs make the perfect quick brunch.

name: Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Mian)
instructions: Cook noodles according to package, drain and set aside.
Fry sliced scallions in oil over medium heat until deep golden and fragrant.
Mix soy sauces and sugar, pour over hot noodles.
Add the scallion oil (with the fried bits) and toss well.
Serve immediately — simple and deeply flavorful.
tips: The key is frying the scallions slowly until they turn crispy and aromatic.

name: Japanese Curry Rice (Home Style)
instructions: Sauté onion, carrot, and potato (and meat if using) until lightly browned.
Add water and simmer until vegetables are soft.
Turn off heat, add curry roux blocks and stir until dissolved.
Simmer gently 5–10 minutes until thickened.
Serve hot over rice.
tips: Store-bought Japanese curry roux makes this extremely easy and authentic-tasting. A true home comfort brunch.

name: Japanese Fruit Sandwich (Fruit Sando)
instructions: Whip cream with a little sugar until stiff.
Spread cream on bread slices.
Arrange cut fruit neatly on one slice.
Top with the other slice, press gently, and wrap tightly.
Chill 30 minutes, then cut and serve.
tips: Use very soft milk bread for the classic Japanese fruit sando texture.

name: Tamago Sando (Japanese Egg Sandwich)
instructions: Boil eggs until just firm, then cool and peel.
Mash eggs with Japanese mayo, salt, and pepper until creamy.
Butter the bread slices lightly.
Spread a thick layer of egg salad between two slices.
Trim crusts if desired, cut in half, and serve.
tips: Japanese mayo is slightly sweeter and richer — it makes the classic konbini-style filling.

name: Matcha Latte French Toast
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, matcha, sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
Soak bread slices in the matcha custard for 30–60 seconds per side.
Cook in a buttered pan over medium-low heat until golden on both sides.
Dust with extra matcha or powdered sugar.
Serve with whipped cream or red bean paste.
tips: Thick milk bread absorbs the custard without falling apart — perfect for a café-style brunch.

name: Ochazuke (Tea Over Rice)

ingredients.name: Optional: salmon flakes, umeboshi, or wasabi

instructions: Place warm rice in a deep bowl.
Add toppings of your choice (salmon, umeboshi, etc.).
Pour hot green tea or dashi over the rice.
Sprinkle with nori and sesame seeds.
Eat immediately while the rice is still hot and the tea is fragrant.
tips: A classic light Japanese brunch or late-night comfort food — extremely simple and soothing.

name: Japanese Potato Salad
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, then mash roughly (leave some chunks).
Salt the cucumber slices and squeeze out excess water.
Mix potatoes with mayo, cucumber, carrot, and chopped egg.
Season with a splash of rice vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Chill briefly and serve as a side or light brunch plate.
tips: Japanese potato salad is creamier and slightly sweeter than Western versions — perfect with rice or as a sandwich filling.

name: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook rice and keep warm.
Sauté each vegetable separately with a pinch of salt.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Arrange rice in bowls, top with vegetables in sections.
Add egg on top, serve with gochujang on the side.
tips: Mix everything together before eating for the best flavor blend.

name: Korean Soft Scrambled Eggs with Rice
instructions: Beat eggs with milk, salt, and white pepper.
Melt butter in a non-stick pan over low heat.
Pour in eggs and stir gently and continuously until soft and creamy (do not brown).
Remove from heat while still slightly runny.
Serve over hot rice, drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle green onion.
tips: Low heat and constant stirring give the classic soft Korean-style scrambled eggs.

name: Gimbap (Korean Seaweed Rice Rolls)
instructions: Season warm rice with sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Lay a nori sheet on a bamboo mat, spread rice thinly leaving a border.
Arrange fillings in a line across the center.
Roll tightly using the mat, seal the edge with a little water.
Slice into bite-sized pieces and arrange on a plate.
tips: Wet your knife between cuts for clean slices. Great make-ahead brunch item.

name: Korean Egg Soup (Gyeran-guk)
instructions: Bring stock to a gentle boil.
Beat eggs and slowly drizzle them into the simmering stock while stirring.
Add green onion and season with salt, sesame oil, and white pepper.
Simmer 1–2 minutes until the egg is just set.
Serve hot as a light, comforting brunch soup.
tips: A classic Korean light soup — very simple and soothing.

name: Kimchi Fried Rice (Kimchi Bokkeumbap)
instructions: Stir-fry kimchi and optional spam in a little oil until fragrant.
Add rice and kimchi juice, breaking up any clumps.
Stir-fry over medium-high heat until the rice is hot and slightly crispy.
Push rice aside, fry an egg, then mix or serve on top.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle green onion.
tips: Day-old rice works best. This is one of the easiest and most satisfying Korean home brunches.

name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
instructions: Soak hard rice cakes in warm water for 10 minutes if needed.
Make a sauce with gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar.
Simmer the sauce with stock, add rice cakes and fish cake.
Cook until the sauce thickens and coats the cakes.
Finish with sliced green onion and serve hot.
tips: A popular Korean snack that works perfectly as a hearty brunch — adjust spice to your liking.

name: Ensaymada
instructions: Make a soft enriched dough and let it rise.
Shape into coils or rounds.
Bake until golden.
Brush with butter, sprinkle with sugar and grated cheese.
Serve warm as a classic Filipino brunch pastry.
tips: The cheese + butter + sugar combination is what makes ensaymada special.

name: Tortang Talong
instructions: Grill or boil eggplants until soft, then peel.
Flatten the eggplant and dip in beaten eggs.
Pan-fry until both sides are golden.
Serve with garlic rice or banana ketchup.
Classic Filipino eggplant omelette.
tips: Some people stuff it with ground meat for a heartier version.

name: Ginataang Bilo-Bilo
instructions: Cook sago until translucent.
Simmer coconut milk with sugar and fruits.
Add glutinous rice balls and cook until they float.
Add sago and simmer until thick.
Serve warm as a sweet Filipino brunch or merienda.
tips: A comforting coconut-based dessert soup perfect for brunch.

name: Longsilog
instructions: Pan-fry longganisa until caramelized and cooked through.
Make garlic fried rice with leftover rice and lots of garlic.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Plate rice, sausages, and egg together.
Serve with sliced tomato and a simple vinegar dip.
tips: A classic silog breakfast-for-brunch plate — savory, garlicky, and satisfying.

name: Spam Silog
instructions: Pan-fry Spam slices until crispy and caramelized on the edges.
Prepare garlic fried rice.
Fry eggs to your liking (sunny-side up is classic).
Plate rice, Spam, and egg together.
Serve with banana ketchup or a simple vinegar dip.
tips: One of the easiest and most popular Filipino home brunch plates — salty, garlicky, and ready in minutes.

name: Turon (Banana Lumpia)
instructions: Slice bananas lengthwise and roll in brown sugar.
Place on a lumpia wrapper with optional jackfruit.
Roll tightly and seal the edge with water.
Deep-fry or pan-fry until golden and caramelized.
Drain and serve warm as a sweet brunch treat.
tips: The sugar caramelizes into a crispy shell — best eaten fresh and still hot.

name: Thai Jok (Rice Porridge)
instructions: Simmer rice in stock until it breaks down into a creamy porridge.
Add seasoned minced pork and cook through.
Ladle into bowls and top with a soft-boiled egg.
Garnish with shredded ginger, green onion, and fried garlic.
Serve with white pepper and soy sauce on the side.
tips: Jok is thicker and creamier than Chinese congee — perfect soothing brunch.

name: Kai Kratha (Thai Pan Eggs)
instructions: Heat small pans with a little oil.
Add sliced Chinese sausage and cook until fragrant.
Crack eggs into the pans and season lightly.
Cook until whites are set but yolks still runny.
Serve sizzling in the pan with rice or toast.
tips: Often served in the same small pan it was cooked in — great for sharing at brunch.

name: Mango Sticky Rice
instructions: Soak and steam sticky rice until tender.
Heat coconut milk with sugar and a pinch of salt.
Pour most of the sweet coconut milk over the hot rice and let it absorb.
Slice ripe mango and arrange beside the rice.
Drizzle remaining coconut sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Use the ripest yellow mangoes you can find — the contrast of creamy rice and sweet fruit is perfect.

name: Thai Garlic Fried Rice with Crispy Egg
instructions: Fry minced garlic in oil over medium heat until golden and fragrant (don’t burn).
Add rice and stir-fry, breaking up clumps. Season with fish sauce and soy sauce.
In a separate pan, fry eggs until the edges are crispy and the yolk is still runny.
Plate the garlic rice and top with the crispy egg.
Serve with sliced cucumber, green onion, and a lime wedge.
tips: Day-old rice and lots of garlic are the secrets. The crispy egg makes it feel special.

name: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Fish sauce + oyster sauce + soy sauce

instructions: Pound garlic and chilies into a rough paste.
Stir-fry the paste in hot oil until fragrant.
Add minced meat and cook until done.
Season with fish sauce, oyster sauce, and a pinch of sugar.
Toss in holy basil until just wilted.
Serve over rice with a fried egg on top.
tips: One of the most popular Thai home dishes — fast, fragrant, and perfect for brunch.

name: Thai Cucumber Salad (Ajad) with Rice
instructions: Slice cucumber and shallot thinly.
Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved.
Toss cucumber, shallot, and chili with the dressing.
Let sit 5–10 minutes so the flavors meld.
Serve alongside or over warm jasmine rice as a light brunch.
tips: A bright, cooling side that balances richer dishes — ready in minutes with almost no cooking.
